bib.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2020 (34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can diffusion probabilistic models generate high-quality images, and which parameterization and objective make them work best?
hypothesis: A parameterization that predicts the noise epsilon, trained with an unweighted simplified bound, links diffusion models to denoising score matching and gives better sample quality.
contributions: Show diffusion models can generate high-quality samples (CIFAR10 FID 3.17, LSUN 256x256 comparable to ProgressiveGAN)
Equivalence of epsilon-prediction diffusion training to denoising score matching over multiple noise levels and sampling to annealed Langevin dynamics
Progressive lossy compression and autoregressive-decoding interpretation

method.summary: A U-Net predicts the noise added to an image at a random timestep t (T=1000, linear beta schedule); training minimises the mean squared error of the noise (Lsimple), and sampling iterates the learned reverse Gaussian chain from pure noise.

datasets.name: CIFAR10
datasets.split: standard from prior generative-modelling papers; FID vs training set (5.24 vs test set)
datasets.preprocessing: integers 0-255 scaled linearly to [-1,1]; random horizontal flips

datasets.name: LSUN Bedroom, Church, Cat 256x256
datasets.preprocessing: random horizontal flips except LSUN Bedroom

models.name: DDPM U-Net (CIFAR10)
models.architecture: PixelCNN++-style Wide ResNet U-Net, group norm, self-attention at 16x16, sinusoidal time embedding in each residual block
models.layers: four feature map resolutions (32x32 to 4x4), two conv residual blocks per level

models.name: DDPM U-Net (256x256)
models.layers: six feature map resolutions, two residual blocks per level

training.objective: Lsimple = E ||eps - eps_theta(sqrt(abar_t) x0 + sqrt(1-abar_t) eps, t)||^2, t uniform in 1..T; reverse variance fixed sigma_t^2 = beta_t (or beta-tilde_t, similar)
training.steps: CIFAR10 800k; CelebA-HQ 0.5M; LSUN Bedroom 2.4M; Cat 1.8M; Church 1.2M; large Bedroom 1.15M
training.regularisation: EMA of parameters, decay 0.9999; random horizontal flips
training.wall_clock: CIFAR10 10.6 hours for 800k steps at 21 steps/s; 256x256 models 2.2 steps/s at batch 64
training.seeds: inferred: single run (trained once and evaluated throughout training)

other.beta schedule: linear from 1e-4 to 0.02, chosen from constant/linear/quadratic
other.checkpoint selection: minimum FID over the course of training

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling, Algorithm 2: x_{t-1} = (x_t - (1-alpha_t)/sqrt(1-abar_t) eps_theta)/sqrt(alpha_t) + sigma_t z

other.sampling cost: CIFAR10 batch 256 in 17 s; 256x256 batch 128 in 300 s

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception distance, TTUR code on CIFAR10, StyleGAN2 code on LSUN, 50000 samples

metrics.name: NLL
metrics.definition: lossless codelength from the variational bound

eval.protocol: single training run, best (minimum) FID over training reported; no confidence intervals other than IS std

code.snippet: Training: x0~q(x0); t~Uniform({1..T}); eps~N(0,I); gradient step on ||eps - eps_theta(sqrt(abar_t) x0 + sqrt(1-abar_t) eps, t)||^2.  Sampling: xT~N(0,I); for t=T..1: z~N(0,I) if t>1 else 0; x_{t-1} = 1/sqrt(alpha_t) (x_t - (1-alpha_t)/sqrt(1-abar_t) eps_theta(x_t,t)) + sigma_t z
